questions.question: Naphthalene balls disappear with time because of _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** ​Sublimation.**__

Sublimation is a change in a state of matter, just like melting, freezing, and evaporation. Through sublimation, a substance changes from a **solid to a gas without ever passing through a liquid phase**.

Example: Dry ice, solid CO2, Naphthalene.

questions.question: What is sublimation?

options.text: direct change of a substance from a gas to a liquid state
direct change of a substance from a gas to a solid state
direct change of a substance from a liquid to a gas state
direct change of a substance from a solid to a gas state

questions.solution:
The correct answer is the __**direct change of a substance from a solid to a gas state.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sublimation** is a process in which a **solid transforms directly into vapours without changing into liquid.**
 
• This phenomenon can be seen in **camphor or naphthalene balls.**
 
• In the process **snow or ice transforms directly into water vapour without becoming water.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

 
• **Deposition** - It is the process of conversion of a gas to a solid.
 
• Evaporation - It is the process of conversion of a liquid into gas.
 
• Fusion/Melting - It is the process of conversion of a solid into a liquid.
 
• Condensation - It is the process of conversion of a gas into a liquid.

questions.question: Intermixing of particles of two different types of matter on their own is called ________
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Diffusion**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Diffusion**: Intermixing of particles of two different types of matter on their own is called diffusion

 
 
• Diffusion is process in which particles of matter get intermixed on their own, this happens due to entrance of particles into the spaces. Diffusion is a result of the kinetic properties of particles of matter. The particles will mix until they are evenly distributed
 
 
 
• **Condensation **is the process where water vapour becomes liquid. It is the reverse of evaporation, where liquid water becomes a vapour.
 
• **Fission**: The splitting of an unstable atomic nucleus into two or more nuclei is known as fission.
 
• **Effusion **refers to the accumulation of fluid in an anatomic space, usually without loculation.

questions.question: _____ is the heat per unit mass required to change a substance from solid into liquid at the same temperature and pressure.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option **2** i.e __**Latent heat of fusion.**__

 
• The latent heat of fusion is the heat per unit mass required to change a substance from solid into liquid at the same temperature and pressure.
 
 
• Latent heat of fusion is also known as the **enthalpy of fusion**.
 
• The latent heat of fusion of a solid is almost always positive in value.

questions.question: Which one of the following takes place when water transforms from liquid to gaseous phase?

options.text: The colour of the particles change.

questions.solution:
__**Explanation:**__

**States of matter**

 
• Matter exists in nature in different forms, the three basic states of matter are **Solid, Liquid and Gas.**
 
• Apart from these three, there are **two more states of matter** exist which we do not see in our everyday life. They are **Plasma & Bose-Einstein condensate.**

**​Properties of Solid -**

 
• In solids, the **particles are closely packed **and the gaps between the particles are tiny and hence it is tough to compress them.
 
• Solid has a **fixed shape and volume. **

**Properties of Liquid -**

 
• In a liquid, particles are **less tightly packed** as compared to solids and less difficult to compress as compare to solid because particles have less space between them to move but more than the that of solid.
 
• **Liquids take the shape of the container in which they are kept.**

**Properties of Gas -**

 
• In gases, particles are far apart from each other, the **force of attraction between the particles is negligible** and they can move freely.
 
• The gaseous state has the highest compressibility as compared to solids and liquids.
 
• Gases have **neither a fixed volume nor a fixed shape.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5dec49010d5005df8db9e8cc01c67aa72acf1ea19240e18de9e95974c37b682e.png] 

When one state of the matter changes to another. The distance between its other particles changes.

Hence, **Solid (Highly packed molecules) → Liquid (Less closely packed molecules) → Gas (Very very less closely packed).**

⇒ When matter **changes from liquid phase to solid phase** the **distance between particles changes.**

questions.question: During hot summer days, water is usually kept in the earthen pot to keep it cool. Which of the following process is used to keep it cool?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option **4** i.e. __**Evaporation.**__

__**Explanation: **__

 
• The earthen pot has a large number of extremely **small pores** in its walls.
 
• Some of the water continuously keeps seeping through those **pores** to the outside of the pot.
 
• This water evaporates continuously and takes the latent heat required for** vaporization** from the earthen pot and the remaining water.
 
• In this way, the remaining water** loses heat **and gets cooled.
 
• This is also an example of **cooling caused by evaporation**.

The four processes provided in the options are explained below:

 
 

 **Phenomenon**
 **Explanations**
 
 

 **Freezing**
 
 
 
• The process of changing a liquid into a solid by cooling is called freezing.
 
• In simple words, freezing means solidification.
 
• It is the reverse of the melting.
 
• The state of matter can be changed by changing that temperature (by heating or cooling).
 
 
 
 

 **Condensation**
 
 
 
• The process of changing a gas (or vapour) to a liquid by cooling, is called condensation.
 
• It is the reverse of boiling or vaporization.
 
• When a gas is cooled enough (by lowering its temperature), then its particle loses so much kinetic energy that they slow down, move closer together until they start being attracted to each other, and form a liquid.
 
 
 
 

 **Sublimation**
 
 
 
• The changing of a solid directly into vapours on heating and of vapours into solid on cooling is known as sublimation.
 
• The changing of a solid directly into vapour (or gas) is called sublimation.
 
• The changing of vapour (or gas) directly into solid is also called sublimation.
 
• The common substances which undergo sublimation are Ammonium chloride, Iodine, Camphor, Naphthalene, and Anthracene.
 
 
 
 

 **Evaporation**
 
 
 
• The process of the liquid changing into vapour even below its boiling point is called** evaporation**.
 
• Whatever be the temperature at which evaporation takes place, the **latent heat of vaporization** must be supplied whenever a liquid changes into a vapour.
